learningObjective: Describe what typically goes into a model deployment package (weights + graph + metadata) and why the packaging boundary matters for reproducibility.
stem: Which is the most complete description of what a well-packaged inference model artifact typically contains?

options.text: Only the weight tensors serialized as a single binary blob; graph structure and signatures are inferred by the runtime at load time by tracing the model on a synthetic input tensor of zeros.
Only the Python source code of the model; runtime re-instantiates and initializes weights from a random seed at deployment because random weights are close enough to the trained ones for inference.

(i) The graph structure or compiled program; (ii) the weight tensors with dtype/shape/layout metadata; (iii) input/output signatures (names, dtypes, shape specs); (iv) preprocessing/postprocessing metadata (tokenizer config, normalization stats, calibration scales for quantized models) — plus a version tag identifying the schema of the archive itself.
Only a URL pointing to the model in the training framework's registry; the runtime downloads weights and code fresh on every process start to guarantee freshness of the artifact.

explanation: A robust deployment artifact contains structure (graph or compiled program), weights (with metadata), signatures, and preprocessing/postprocessing metadata, plus an archive version. Options A/B/D describe non-viable packaging schemes: shipping only weights would leave graph and pre/postprocessing undefined; shipping only source and random-initializing weights is nonsensical; downloading on every start couples deployment to network availability and defeats reproducibility.

optionExplanations.B: Wrong: random init is not equivalent to trained weights.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: matches standard packaging (SavedModel, TorchScript, ONNX, safetensors + config).

assumptions: Production deployment where reproducibility, portability and offline operation matter.
nonImplications: Does not imply a single format fits every use case; the LLM community often uses safetensors + tokenizer config + generation config as multiple files rather than one bundle.
Does not imply preprocessing metadata is always separable from the model; some vendors embed it in the compiled artifact.
